input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-Readiness Gap Assessment

## Description

This epic delivers the definitive GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack,
inventorying the gaps between current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar
across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling. It
produces the GA scope document that determines what the hardening work must
close before graduation. This is the strategy's P0 foundation: until it lands,
the size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

## Scope

- Systematically inventory gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar in
  four enumerated areas: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error
  handling.
- Consolidate TP feedback scattered across support tickets into the gap
  inventory.
- Assess the current state of the Llama Stack distribution (API surface,
  LlamaStackDistribution CR lifecycle, provider integrations) against GA
  expectations for each area.
- Produce the definitive GA scope: a prioritized, gap-by-gap inventory with a
  recommended disposition for each gap (must-fix for GA, deferred, or
  already-met), forming the re-baselined scope for the hardening work that
  follows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The assessment report inventories gaps in all four areas (API stability,
  upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling) with each gap stated
  concretely enough to be scheduled as remediation work.
- Every gap entry carries a disposition: must-fix for GA, deferred with
  rationale, or already-met with evidence.
- TP feedback from support tickets is reflected in the inventory (each
  recurring TP complaint category maps to a gap entry or an explicit
  already-met/deferred disposition).
- The report identifies a definitive GA scope that the downstream hardening
  work can be re-baselined against, and is reviewed and accepted by the
  owning team.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: This epic delivers the GA-readiness assessment that
  inventories the gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar, producing
  the definitive GA scope.

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantees and Tested TP Upgrade Path

## Description

This epic puts a stability guarantee on the published Llama Stack API surface:
versioned APIs, a documented deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path
from the last two Tech Preview releases. It delivers the HLR-2 portion of the
GA graduation — the commitment enterprise customers need before building
production GenAI applications on the component.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published Llama Stack API surface exposed
  by the distribution (OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the
  LlamaStackDistribution CRD surface as configured by the distribution).
- Define and document a deprecation policy: how API changes are versioned,
  announced, and retired, and what support window deprecated surfaces keep.
- Build and automate an upgrade-path test that verifies a distribution
  deployed on each of the last two TP releases upgrades to the GA release
  with documented, non-breaking behavior for the supported surface.
- Ensure the deprecation policy and versioning scheme are applied
  consistently across the published API surface.
- Scope boundary: this epic delivers only the enumerated stability machinery
  above. Any additional API-stability gap the GA-readiness assessment
  inventories is remediated in the assessment-findings remediation work, not
  here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, and the versioning is visible and
  documented in the API surface the distribution exposes.
- A deprecation policy document exists stating versioning, announcement, and
  retirement rules for API changes, approved by the owning team.
- An automated upgrade-path test exists and passes for upgrades from each of
  the last two TP releases to the GA release, covering the supported
  configuration surface.
- No breaking change to the published, supported API surface is introduced
  without following the deprecation policy (verified by the upgrade-path
  test and API surface review).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee —
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases. Full coverage of this HLR.

# Remediate Llama Stack GA-Readiness Gaps

## Description

This epic closes the quality gaps that the GA-readiness assessment
inventories — the hardening work that Tech Preview status currently excuses,
centered on scale limits and error handling plus any additional findings the
assessment produces. Its scope is re-baselined against the assessment's
definitive GA scope: until the assessment lands, the size of this work is an
estimate.

## Description of Dependency

This epic cannot start until the GA-readiness assessment has produced the
definitive GA scope; the assessment's findings determine what this epic must
fix. If the assessment finds no gaps beyond the explicitly required API
stability and support-posture work, this epic reduces to remediating only the
specific findings; if it finds materially more, the epic is re-split along
gap-category lines (see the decomposition summary's health warnings).

## Scope

- Remediate the must-fix gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment,
  including scale limits (documented and enforced limits for supported
  distribution sizes and workloads) and error handling (actionable, consistent
  error behavior across the published API surface).
- Ownership boundary with the API-stability work: the enumerated stability
  machinery — API versioning, the deprecation policy, and the automated
  upgrade-path test from the last two Tech Preview releases — is delivered by
  the API-stability epic. Any API-stability gap the assessment inventories
  beyond that enumerated machinery (for example, undocumented surface
  behavior or inconsistent error contracts on specific endpoints) is
  remediated in this epic, not there.
- Re-baseline this epic's backlog against the assessment's gap inventory at
  the start of execution: each must-fix gap becomes a tracked work item here.
- Verify that remediated gaps meet the GA bar as stated by the assessment's
  dispositions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every gap the assessment dispositioned as must-fix for GA has a completed,
  verified remediation tracked in this epic's work items.
- Scale limits supported by the distribution are enforced and documented
  (behavior at the limit is defined and tested).
- Error handling across the published API surface is consistent and
  actionable per the assessment's error-handling findings, verified by tests
  covering the failure modes the assessment identified.
- The remediation work is validated against the assessment report: no
  must-fix gap remains open at completion.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: Delivers the closure of the gaps the GA-readiness
  assessment inventories — the assessment (tracked separately) produces the
  definitive GA scope; this epic closes the must-fix items in it.

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture required for GA:
documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration
matrix for Llama Stack distributions. It delivers the HLR-3 portion of the
GA graduation — the operational commitments that distinguish a supported
component from a Tech Preview one.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the supported aspects of Llama Stack
  distributions (e.g. API availability and latency expectations appropriate
  to the component's role), stated measurably enough for support to act on.
- Define and document a backport policy: which releases receive fixes, for
  how long, and how backports are requested and delivered.
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix: the distribution
  configurations, provider integrations (e.g. the default inference
  provider), and versions the component commits to supporting at GA.
- Align the posture documents with the platform's existing GA support
  conventions and get them ratified by the owning team and support
  stakeholders.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented SLO target set exists for the supported distribution surface,
  reviewed and accepted by the owning team and support stakeholders.
- A backport policy document exists stating supported release lines, backport
  criteria, and request/delivery process.
- A supported configuration matrix exists enumerating the configurations and
  provider integrations supported at GA, with unsupported combinations
  explicitly marked.
- The three posture artifacts are published where support and customers can
  reference them, and consistent with one another (no SLO or backport claim
  contradicting the configuration matrix).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place — documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. Full coverage
  of this HLR.

# Promote TrustyAI Guardrails to a Supported Integration in Llama Stack Distributions

## Description

This epic promotes Llama Stack's TrustyAI safety-guardrails integration from
an experimental flag to a supported, documented integration available in GA
Llama Stack distributions. TrustyAI itself is already a Stable (GA) platform
component providing guardrails services; the change is on the Llama Stack
distribution side — making the integration a first-class supported option
rather than an experimental opt-in — and validating it jointly with the
TrustyAI service.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental status of the TrustyAI guardrails integration in
  Llama Stack distributions: the integration is available and supported in
  GA distributions without an experimental opt-in flag.
- Wire the integration so it follows the distribution's established provider/
  integration configuration patterns rather than an experimental side
  channel.
- Validate the integration end-to-end with the TrustyAI service: guardrails
  requests from a Llama Stack distribution are served by TrustyAI as
  documented, with defined behavior when the TrustyAI service is unavailable.
- Obtain TrustyAI-team sign-off that the integration is supportable as a
  supported combination (TrustyAI is owned by a separate team; the
  integration must be validated from both sides).
- Document the integration's supported status as part of the GA documentation
  effort (content delivered there; this epic supplies the validated
  integration and the technical facts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA Llama Stack distribution can be configured with TrustyAI guardrails
  without any experimental flag, using the distribution's supported
  configuration surface.
- An end-to-end validation demonstrates guardrails requests flowing from a
  Llama Stack distribution to the TrustyAI service and behaving as
  documented, including defined failure behavior when TrustyAI is
  unavailable.
- The TrustyAI team has signed off that the integration is supportable as a
  supported combination (no open objections from the TrustyAI side).
- The integration is covered by the distribution's automated tests so
  regressions in the integration are caught.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. Full coverage
  of this HLR; the documentation half is completed by the GA documentation
  effort using this epic's validated integration.

# Enable Llama Stack Management by Default in the Dashboard for Entitled Clusters

## Description

This epic makes Llama Stack management available by default in the Dashboard
for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. It delivers the
HLR-5 portion of the GA graduation on the Dashboard side, driven by the
Dashboard's per-component feature flags and defaults.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management enablement from an opt-in
  (TP gate) to enabled-by-default behavior for entitled clusters, following
  the Dashboard's existing feature-flag and default-configuration patterns.
- Gate default enablement on cluster entitlement so only entitled clusters
  get Llama Stack management surfaced by default; non-entitled clusters see
  the existing behavior.
- Cover the default-enabled path with the Dashboard's standard views
  (navigation, resource surfaces) for Llama Stack management, consistent with
  how other GA components are surfaced.
- Update Dashboard tests covering the default-on entitlement path and the
  non-entitled path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with no explicit opt-in configuration, Llama Stack
  management surfaces are available in the Dashboard by default.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management is not surfaced by
  default (existing behavior preserved).
- Automated Dashboard tests cover both the entitled default-enabled path and
  the non-entitled path, and pass.
- No TP opt-in gate remains in the Dashboard's Llama Stack enablement path.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). Full coverage of this HLR.

# GA Documentation Uplift and TP Migration Notes for Llama Stack

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards and adds
migration notes from Tech Preview, so customers moving from TP distributions
to the GA release have an authoritative path. It is a `docs-authoring` epic:
content work through the Red Hat docs process, technically reviewed against
what was actually built.

## Scope

- Audit existing Llama Stack documentation against GA standards and uplift it
  (accuracy, completeness, supported-usage guidance consistent with the GA
  support posture and supported configuration matrix).
- Author migration notes from Tech Preview: what changes between the last TP
  releases and the GA release, including API stability/deprecation policy
  effects on existing TP deployments and the tested upgrade path.
- Document the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration and the
  default-enabled Dashboard management behavior as part of the GA
  documentation set.
- Content outline (topics to be authored or rewritten):
  - GA readiness and support posture overview (SLOs, backport policy,
    supported configuration matrix, as published by the support-posture work)
  - Upgrade and migration from TP releases (migration notes, deprecated
    surfaces, upgrade path)
  - Supported TrustyAI guardrails integration usage
  - Dashboard management of Llama Stack distributions (default-enabled for
    entitled clusters)
  - Any gap-remediation behavior changes surfaced to users (scale limits,
    error handling) identified by the GA-readiness assessment's remediation

## Acceptance Criteria

- Llama Stack documentation meets GA standards as accepted by the docs
  review: no TP-era caveats left on supported surfaces, supported usage is
  accurately described.
- Migration notes from TP exist and cover the differences between the last
  two TP releases and GA, including deprecated API surfaces per the
  deprecation policy.
- Documentation for the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration and
  default-enabled Dashboard management is published.
- All content is technically reviewed against the implemented GA behavior
  (API stability work, support posture, guardrails integration, Dashboard
  enablement, gap remediation) by the owning engineers, with review sign-off
  recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-6 (P2)**: Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including
  migration notes from TP. Full coverage of this HLR.
